findings.summary: The truncation note says 'dropped the first N bytes, kept the last <cap>'. Runners pass in N as the stdout and stderr drops added together (and in claude-code, also the bytes of discarded unterminated stdout lines). If both streams overflow, or claude-code throws away a long line, no single stream had 'the first N bytes' dropped. The note is wrong but nothing else breaks. Consider wording it as a total across streams.

findings.summary: Once claude-code discards a long unterminated line, the rest of that line from the next chunk becomes a new partial line. Its bytes are not counted in droppedStdoutBytes unless that piece also exceeds the cap. The JSON parse then fails and the line is ignored, so results are unaffected. outputTruncatedBytes can undercount slightly.

findings.summary: Behaviour change worth noting in the docs or PR body. The Claude Code child runs with the Bash tool, so commands it runs (pnpm test, build tools) now lose variables such as CI, NODE_OPTIONS, JAVA_HOME and NPM_CONFIG_*. GitHubActionsRunner also loses CI=true. This is intended; the operator restores any of them with AI_SDLC_RUNNER_ENV_PASSTHROUGH. Consider listing CI in the base allow-list or calling out this effect in adapter-authoring.md.

findings.summary: Every AI_SDLC_* variable is passed to the child unless its name matches /TOKEN|SECRET|KEY|PASSWORD|CREDENTIAL/i. The repo has a GitHub PAT named AI_SDLC_PAT (orchestrator/src/cli/commands/setup.ts:314, init-templates.ts:594-634), and that name matches none of those words. If an operator or a CI job exports AI_SDLC_PAT where the orchestrator runs, buildRunnerEnv hands that GitHub write token to every third-party agent CLI (cursor, codex, claude-code). That is the exposure this task exists to remove. It is minor because the documented use keeps AI_SDLC_PAT inside a single workflow step's env, not the orchestrator's. Suggested fix: add PAT|PRIVATE|AUTH to SECRET_NAME, or list the safe AI_SDLC_* names explicitly instead of trying to catch the secret ones.
